issues.legal_issue: In a title suit challenging an earlier transfer as sham and unsupported by consideration, the court may decide the issue by considering all evidence tendered by both sides despite the plaintiff bearing the burden of proof.
material_facts: The plaintiff claimed title under a later deed and alleged that an earlier deed to the defendant was sham, unsupported by consideration, and inoperative.
The plaintiff bore the burden of establishing that the earlier deed was sham and unsupported by consideration.
Both sides tendered evidence on the deed, including consideration and possession, and the lower appellate court assessed the whole record.
issues.conclusion: Because both sides had tendered evidence, the court was entitled to consider all of it; the defendant could not ask the court to disregard evidence the defendant had chosen to present. The lower appellate court did not err in its approach to the burden of proof.
issues.legal_principle: In a suit based on title, the plaintiff bears the burden of proving title and, when relying on the invalidity of an earlier deed by the same vendor, must establish that it was sham and unsupported by consideration. Once both parties have tendered evidence, the court must consider all material evidence; the question of burden at the end of the case is not of great importance. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.title_suit_challenges_prior_transfer: The plaintiff brought a title suit and challenged an earlier transfer of the same property.
predicates.plaintiff_bears_burden_to_prove_invalidi: The plaintiff relied on the claim that the earlier transfer was sham and unsupported by consideration to establish title.
predicates.both_sides_tender_evidence: Both the plaintiff and the defendant presented evidence concerning the earlier transfer.

issues.definition: When a title suit challenges an earlier transfer and both sides present evidence, the court may consider all of that evidence.

issues.legal_issue: A second appeal does not require interference when the lower appellate court applies the correct burden of proof, assesses the entire evidence, and records factual findings supported by the record.
material_facts: After remand, the lower appellate court considered the plaintiff’s burden to prove the earlier deed sham and unsupported by consideration.
The lower appellate court assessed evidence concerning the parties’ relationship, custody and preparation of the deed, consideration, motive, and possession.
It found the evidence supporting payment of consideration unsatisfactory, found the plaintiff’s account supported, and concluded that the earlier deed created no title or possession.
The High Court dismissed the second appeal in limine, and the Supreme Court found no error in the lower appellate court’s approach or findings.
issues.conclusion: The lower appellate court’s findings were factual, based on a clear analysis of the entire evidence, and supported by the record; the High Court did not err in dismissing the second appeal, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the asserted error in the lower appellate court’s approach was examined, but its findings were factual and supported by the evidence after it applied the proper burden of proof. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.second_appeal_from_fact_findings: The proceeding is a second appeal challenging findings made by a lower appellate court.
predicates.lower_appellate_court_applies_correct_bu: The lower appellate court treats the plaintiff as bearing the burden of proving the challenged transfer invalid.
predicates.lower_appellate_court_assesses_entire_re: The lower appellate court evaluates the evidence presented by both sides.
predicates.findings_supported_by_record: The lower appellate court’s factual findings are supported by its analysis of the evidence.

issues.definition: A second appeal challenging factual findings may be dismissed when the lower appellate court applies the correct burden, considers the whole record, and makes findings supported by that record.
